newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Surge of foreign funds boost Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: Surge of foreign funds boost Singapore stocks.

text.p: A surge of foreign funds in the afternoon boosted an otherwise sedate Singapore stock market to end firmer in hectic trade on Friday, dealers said.

An inflow of foreign funds from the United States and the United Kingdom resulted in a flurry of activity in the afternoon which saw volumes rise to a feverish pitch of over 327 million shares, a daily level unseen for over a year.

"About US$100 million from the U.S. were channelled through two U.S. houses to be pumped into various blue chips in Singapore such as property and banking stocks," said a dealer with one of the U.S. houses.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 23.85 points, or 1.07 percent, up at 2,244.21 after hitting a low of 2,220.36, led by property and banking counters. Gainers outpaced losers by 307 to 90.
Foreign funds were increasing their exposure in Singapore to diversify their portfolios, said dealers. This fuelled the SES property index up 27 points, or 3.77 percent, to 743.65.

Foreign tranches of Singapore Press, OCBC, CityDev led gainers, rising S$0.70-0.90 while Great Eastern shed S$0.40. Small-capitalised stocks and Malaysian stocks led actives on retail interests and speculation. -- Angela Tan (8703083)
